checks.name: cubicPerturbation
checks.code:
/-- The coupled spring potential plus the cubic `x₀³`. -/
noncomputable def cubicPerturbation (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) : ℝ :=
  couplingPotential x + (x 0) ^ 3
checks.doc: The coupled spring potential plus the cubic `x₀³`.

checks.name: cube_iteratedFDeriv_two_zero
checks.code:
/-- The cubic `x₀³` has zero second derivative at the origin. -/
lemma cube_iteratedFDeriv_two_zero (a b : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) => (x 0) ^ 3) 0 ![a, b] = 0 := by
  have hcomp : (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) => (x 0) ^ 3)
      = (fun t : ℝ => t ^ 3) ∘ (EuclideanSpace.proj (𝕜 := ℝ) (0 : Fin 2)) := rfl
  have hcd : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (fun t : ℝ => t ^ 3) := contDiff_id.pow 3
  rw [hcomp, (EuclideanSpace.proj (𝕜 := ℝ) (0 : Fin 2)).iteratedFDeriv_comp_right hcd _ le_top]
  simp [iteratedFDeriv_apply_eq_iteratedDeriv_mul_prod, iteratedDeriv_pow]
checks.doc: The cubic `x₀³` has zero second derivative at the origin.

checks.name: cubicPerturbation_iteratedFDeriv_two_zero
checks.code:
/-- At the origin the second derivative of the perturbed potential is that of the coupled
spring potential. -/
lemma cubicPerturbation_iteratedFDeriv_two_zero (a b : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 cubicPerturbation 0 ![a, b]
      = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 couplingPotential 0 ![a, b] := by
  have hU : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 couplingPotential (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
    (couplingPotential_analyticAt 0).contDiffAt
  have hg : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) => (x 0) ^ 3) 0 :=
    ((EuclideanSpace.proj (𝕜 := ℝ) (0 : Fin 2)).contDiff.pow 3).contDiffAt
  have hsplit : cubicPerturbation
      = couplingPotential + fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) => (x 0) ^ 3 := rfl
  rw [hsplit, iteratedFDeriv_add_apply hU hg]
  simp [cube_iteratedFDeriv_two_zero]
checks.doc: At the origin the second derivative of the perturbed potential is that of the coupled spring potential.

checks.name: cubicPerturbation_analyticAt
checks.code:
/-- The perturbed potential is analytic at every point. -/
lemma cubicPerturbation_analyticAt (z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    AnalyticAt ℝ cubicPerturbation z := by
  have h0 : AnalyticAt ℝ (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) => x 0) z :=
    (EuclideanSpace.proj (𝕜 := ℝ) 0).analyticAt z
  show AnalyticAt ℝ (fun x => couplingPotential x + (x 0) ^ 3) z
  exact (couplingPotential_analyticAt z).add (h0.pow 3)
checks.doc: The perturbed potential is analytic at every point.

checks.name: cubicPerturbation_gradient_zero
checks.code:
/-- The gradient of the perturbed potential vanishes at the origin. -/
lemma cubicPerturbation_gradient_zero :
    gradient cubicPerturbation (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) = 0 := by
  have h0 : HasFDerivAt (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) => x 0)
      (EuclideanSpace.proj (𝕜 := ℝ) 0) (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
    (EuclideanSpace.proj (𝕜 := ℝ) 0).hasFDerivAt
  have hz : ∀ i : Fin 2, (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) i = 0 := fun i => rfl
  have hzero : HasFDerivAt cubicPerturbation (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) →L[ℝ] ℝ) 0 := by
    refine ((couplingPotential_hasFDerivAt 0).add (h0.pow 3)).congr_fderiv ?_
    simp only [hz]
    simp
  simp [gradient, hzero.fderiv]
checks.doc: The gradient of the perturbed potential vanishes at the origin.

checks.name: cubicPerturbation_posDef
checks.code:
/-- The second-derivative quadratic map of the perturbed potential is positive definite at
the origin. -/
lemma cubicPerturbation_posDef :
    (iteratedFDerivQuadraticMap cubicPerturbation (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))).PosDef := by
  intro y hy
  have h0 : (!₂[0, 0] : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) = 0 := by
    ext i
    fin_cases i <;> simp
  have hU := couplingPotential_posDef y hy
  rw [h0] at hU
  show 0 < iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 cubicPerturbation 0 ![y, y]
  rw [cubicPerturbation_iteratedFDeriv_two_zero]
  exact hU
checks.doc: The second-derivative quadratic map of the perturbed potential is positive definite at the origin.

checks.name: cubicPerturbation_isLocalMin
checks.code:
/-- Adding `x₀³` keeps a local minimum at the origin. The proof applies the analytic
second-derivative test from PhyslibAlpha, the test that proves the original theorem. -/
theorem cubicPerturbation_isLocalMin :
    IsLocalMin cubicPerturbation (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :=
  second_derivative_test_analyticAt cubicPerturbation_gradient_zero
    (cubicPerturbation_analyticAt 0) cubicPerturbation_posDef
checks.doc: Adding `x₀³` keeps a local minimum at the origin. The proof applies the analytic second-derivative test from PhyslibAlpha, the test that proves the original theorem.

checks.name: cubicPerturbation_strict_near_origin
checks.code:
/-- Near the origin the minimum is strict: if `|x₀| < 1/4` and `x ≠ 0`, the perturbed
potential is positive, because it is at least `(x₁ + x₀/2)² + x₀²/2`. -/
theorem cubicPerturbation_strict_near_origin :
    ∀ᶠ x in nhds (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
      x ≠ 0 → cubicPerturbation 0 < cubicPerturbation x := by
  have hc : Continuous (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) => x 0) :=
    (EuclideanSpace.proj (𝕜 := ℝ) (0 : Fin 2)).continuous
  have ht : Filter.Tendsto (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) => x 0) (nhds 0) (nhds 0) := by
    simpa using hc.tendsto (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
  have hnear : ∀ᶠ x in nhds (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), |x 0| < 1 / 4 := by
    filter_upwards [ht.eventually (Metric.ball_mem_nhds (0 : ℝ) (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 4))]
      with x hx
    simpa [Metric.mem_ball, Real.dist_eq] using hx
  filter_upwards [hnear] with x hx hne
  have hW0 : cubicPerturbation (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) = 0 := by
    simp [cubicPerturbation, couplingPotential]
  rw [hW0]
  have hlo : -(1 / 4 : ℝ) < x 0 := (abs_lt.mp hx).1
  have hprod : 0 ≤ (x 0) ^ 2 * (x 0 + 1 / 4) := mul_nonneg (sq_nonneg _) (by linarith)
  have hbound : (x 1 + x 0 / 2) ^ 2 + (x 0) ^ 2 / 2 ≤ cubicPerturbation x := by
    unfold cubicPerturbation couplingPotential
    nlinarith [hprod]
  by_contra hlt
  have hle : cubicPerturbation x ≤ 0 := not_lt.mp hlt
  have hs : 0 ≤ (x 1 + x 0 / 2) ^ 2 := sq_nonneg _
  have h0 : x 0 = 0 := by
    have h0sq : (x 0) ^ 2 = 0 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x 0)]
    exact (pow_eq_zero_iff two_ne_zero).mp h0sq
  have h1 : x 1 = 0 := by
    have h1sq : (x 1 + x 0 / 2) ^ 2 = 0 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x 0)]
    have h1lin : x 1 + x 0 / 2 = 0 := (pow_eq_zero_iff two_ne_zero).mp h1sq
    linarith
  apply hne
  ext i
  fin_cases i
  · simpa using h0
  · simpa using h1
checks.doc: Near the origin the minimum is strict: if `|x₀| < 1/4` and `x ≠ 0`, the perturbed potential is positive, because it is at least `(x₁ + x₀/2)² + x₀²/2`.

checks.name: cubicPerturbation_not_global
checks.code:
/-- The origin is not a global minimum after adding `x₀³`: the value at `(-2, 0)` is `-4`. -/
theorem cubicPerturbation_not_global :
    cubicPerturbation (!₂[-2, 0] : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
      < cubicPerturbation (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) := by
  simp [cubicPerturbation, couplingPotential]
  norm_num
checks.doc: The origin is not a global minimum after adding `x₀³`: the value at `(-2, 0)` is `-4`.

checks.name: couplingPotential_eq_sq_add_sq
checks.code:
/-- The coupled spring potential equals `(x₀ + x₁/2)² + (3/4) x₁²` at every point. -/
theorem couplingPotential_eq_sq_add_sq (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    couplingPotential x = (x 0 + x 1 / 2) ^ 2 + 3 / 4 * (x 1) ^ 2 := by
  unfold couplingPotential
  ring
checks.doc: The coupled spring potential equals `(x₀ + x₁/2)² + (3/4) x₁²` at every point.

checks.name: couplingPotential_origin
checks.code:
/-- The coupled spring potential is zero at the origin. -/
theorem couplingPotential_origin :
    couplingPotential (!₂[0, 0] : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) = 0 := by
  first
    | simp [couplingPotential]
    | norm_num [couplingPotential]
checks.doc: The coupled spring potential is zero at the origin.

checks.name: couplingPotential_origin_le
checks.code:
/-- At every point the coupled spring potential is at least its value at the origin. -/
theorem couplingPotential_origin_le (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    couplingPotential (!₂[0, 0] : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) ≤ couplingPotential x := by
  rw [couplingPotential_origin, couplingPotential_eq_sq_add_sq]
  positivity
checks.doc: At every point the coupled spring potential is at least its value at the origin.

checks.name: couplingPotential_pos
checks.code:
/-- Away from the origin the coupled spring potential is strictly positive. -/
theorem couplingPotential_pos (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    0 < couplingPotential x := by
  rw [couplingPotential_eq_sq_add_sq]
  by_contra h
  have hs : 0 ≤ (x 0 + x 1 / 2) ^ 2 := sq_nonneg _
  have ht : 0 ≤ (x 1) ^ 2 := sq_nonneg _
  have h1 : x 1 = 0 := by
    have h1sq : (x 1) ^ 2 = 0 := by linarith
    exact (pow_eq_zero_iff two_ne_zero).mp h1sq
  have h0 : x 0 = 0 := by
    have h0sq : (x 0 + x 1 / 2) ^ 2 = 0 := by linarith
    have h0lin : x 0 + x 1 / 2 = 0 := (pow_eq_zero_iff two_ne_zero).mp h0sq
    linarith
  apply hx
  ext i
  fin_cases i
  · first
      | simpa using h0
      | (simp; exact h0)
      | exact h0
  · first
      | simpa using h1
      | (simp; exact h1)
      | exact h1
checks.doc: Away from the origin the coupled spring potential is strictly positive.

checks.name: couplingPotential_origin_lt
checks.code:
/-- At every point other than the origin the coupled spring potential is larger than at the
origin. -/
theorem couplingPotential_origin_lt (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    couplingPotential (!₂[0, 0] : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) < couplingPotential x := by
  rw [couplingPotential_origin]
  exact couplingPotential_pos x hx
checks.doc: At every point other than the origin the coupled spring potential is larger than at the origin.

checks.name: isLocalMin_of_posDef_of_littleo_without_smoothness
checks.code:
/-- The little-o form of the second-derivative test holds without the smoothness hypothesis:
the proof of `isLocalMin_of_posDef_of_littleo` with its use of that hypothesis removed. -/
theorem isLocalMin_of_posDef_of_littleo_without_smoothness {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] {f : V → ℝ} {x₀ : V}
    (h : (fun x => f x - ∑ i ∈ range 3, 1 / (i)! * iteratedFDeriv ℝ i f x₀ fun _ => x - x₀)
      =o[nhds x₀] fun x => ‖x - x₀‖ ^ 2) (h₀ : gradient f x₀ = 0)
    (hf : (iteratedFDerivQuadraticMap f x₀).PosDef) : IsLocalMin f x₀ := by
  have ⟨C,hC⟩ := coercive_of_posdef hf
  simp only [Asymptotics.IsLittleO, Asymptotics.IsBigOWith] at h
  apply (h (half_pos hC.1)).mono
  intro x
  have hx := hC.2 (x - x₀)
  simp only [continuousBilinearMapOfContinuousMultilinearMap, MultilinearMap.toFun_eq_coe,
    coe_coe, ContinuousLinearMap.coe_mk', LinearMap.coe_mk,
    AddHom.coe_mk] at hx
  rw [mul_assoc,show ![x - x₀, x - x₀] = fun _ => x - x₀ by
    ext i; fin_cases i <;> simp] at hx
  have hx₀ : inner ℝ (gradient f x₀) (x - x₀) = fderiv ℝ f x₀ (x - x₀) := by simp [gradient]
  simp only [h₀, inner_zero_left, map_sub] at hx₀
  simp only [norm_pow, norm_norm]
  rw [← pow_two] at hx
  exact le_of_littleO hx <| sub_eq_zero.mp hx₀.symm
checks.doc: The little-o form of the second-derivative test holds without the smoothness hypothesis: the proof of `isLocalMin_of_posDef_of_littleo` with its use of that hypothesis removed.
